value_unit: structural config corruption quarantine preserving forensic bytes
decision_rationale: The prior pass adopted Aether's private atomic write but did not promote its corrupt-state quarantine. LumiNet now adopts only the structurally-invalid JSON recovery primitive: the exact damaged bytes are moved aside collision-safely, the load still errors, and secret/provider failures are never quarantined as if they were corruption.
invariant: structurally invalid active config bytes are preserved before any later rewrite and the caller still fails closed
negative_invariant: never quarantine on secret-store/provider failures and never overwrite older corrupt evidence
operator_surface: config load error names quarantine path

value_unit: host CPU/memory evidence as a non-amplifying concurrency ceiling
decision_rationale: The earlier objection was opaque hardware-driven behavior. The target-native version is only an upper envelope intersected with each owner's existing limit, so it cannot increase work. It lowers high-fanout diagnostics on constrained hosts and leaves the four-worker subscription ceiling intact.
invariant: host-derived policy may only reduce concurrent work relative to subsystem ceilings
negative_invariant: hardware detection never raises a subsystem ceiling or becomes a scheduler
migration_impact: runtime concurrency may reduce on constrained hosts

value_unit: bounded subscription source mirrors with static admission and per-source fallback
decision_rationale: The donor catalog demonstrates multiple interchangeable feed sources. LumiNet recomposes that value into ProfileService rather than importing donor URLs: one authoritative primary plus at most three deduplicated HTTPS mirrors, per-source health/backoff, and failover. Storage admission shares the egress syntax boundary; runtime still resolves public addresses before network I/O.
invariant: primary source remains authoritative while mirrors are bounded alternatives with independent health and no unsafe egress
negative_invariant: no HTTP/userinfo/non-443 source storage, no TLS downgrade, no mirror promotion into authoritative primary
migration_impact: additive profile fields; in-memory service state only
license_note: data/pattern provenance retained; donor endpoints are not copied

value_unit: last successful source preference inside authoritative ProfileService
decision_rationale: The donor's standalone last-connection file remains a weaker state owner. Its useful ordering primitive is extracted into ProfileService: a still-configured, backoff-eligible last successful source is tried first, while the authoritative primary field never changes.
invariant: last-good preference is advisory ordering only and must refer to a still-configured eligible source
negative_invariant: no duplicate last-connection file and no implicit rewrite of the primary source

value_unit: signed update admission separated from download/install authority
decision_rationale: The four updater/distribution families reveal a useful higher-level plane only after discovery is separated from promotion. LumiNet adds signed manifest admission using configured Ed25519 trust roots, exact current build binding, artifact identity/size/validity bounds and rollback identity, but returns a dry-run plan with apply_authorized=false. There is no downloader or installer.
invariant: only a valid trusted signature bound to the daemon actual current version can produce a bounded non-authoritative plan
negative_invariant: admission never downloads, installs, executes or grants apply authority; client claims cannot choose current version
migration_impact: additive public trust-root config and planning endpoint
license_note: cross-donor behavior rederived target-native; no updater implementation copied

value_unit: read-only host-network mutation preview attached to authoritative transaction owner
decision_rationale: The donor status/preview workflow becomes safe only because the target already owns exact apply, snapshot, rollback and crash recovery. Preview calls the same validation/state observation owner, reports rollback/recovery properties, sets apply_authorized=false, and creates no durable mutation records.
invariant: preview reflects owner-observed state and requested change while remaining side-effect free
negative_invariant: preview never acquires mutation authority, writes recovery state, or changes host DNS/proxy/NCSI/routes

value_unit: automatic mutation retry only under target-owned replay-safety proof
decision_rationale: Fourth-order review reconfirms the donor blind-registration loop remains unsafe while the second-order target solution is complete: per-operation classification, bounded retry, Retry-After saturation, cancellation rebinding, reconciliation before replay, and single-attempt protection.
invariant: every automatic replay is justified by idempotency or successful owner reconciliation
negative_invariant: generic retry never grants authority to replay non-idempotent remote creation
migration_impact: no new runtime change; fourth-order revalidation of live second-order owner

value_unit: bounded redacted per-source failure health and backoff
decision_rationale: The donor concise fetch-error idea is promoted without its unsafe downloader. LumiNet records bounded/redacted errors per configured source, drives exponential eligibility backoff, and retains aggregate profile health for compatibility.
invariant: each source failure retains bounded non-secret diagnostic context and independently influences eligibility
negative_invariant: diagnostic formatting never weakens TLS/SSRF policy or exposes full credential-bearing URLs

value_unit: bounded operator log viewer now superseded by target live UI
decision_rationale: The former reference is no longer a gap: the live control UI already has a 500-line operational log view with refresh/clear and telemetry subscription, so importing donor UI would duplicate a stronger target owner.
invariant: client log history remains bounded and non-authoritative
negative_invariant: no duplicate donor log store or unbounded accumulation

value_unit: allocation-bounded line reader generalized from the donor partial-line bound
decision_rationale: The donor PTY plane is still superseded, but its MAX_PARTIAL invariant exposed a smaller reusable safety primitive. LumiNet replaces unbounded line accumulation at several peer-controlled control/proxy seams with one foundation reader that enforces caller-selected byte ceilings, returns no oversized partial payload, and leaves parsing/lifecycle authority with each protocol owner.
invariant: line-oriented peer input cannot allocate without a caller-defined byte ceiling while waiting for a terminator
negative_invariant: oversized lines are never forwarded as partial payloads and callers must fail the protocol/connection path rather than resume on a desynchronized stream
migration_impact: oversized proxy/Tor/control lines now fail closed instead of accumulating indefinitely
license_note: behavioral invariant extracted and independently reimplemented; donor PTY code not copied
